models.name: icefall streaming Zipformer English (int8, Apache-2.0)
models.note: Fully permissive alternative to the NVIDIA-licensed default: Apache-2.0 weights from icefall, so an Apache-2.0-only deployment can pair it with a WeSpeaker embedder. Trained on LibriSpeech read speech, so expect worse accuracy on real meeting audio (noise, cross-talk, spontaneous speech) than the Nemotron default; unmeasured here.

speakerModels.name: NVIDIA TitaNet-small speaker embedding (192-dim)
speakerModels.measured: 2026-08-12, native 16 kHz meeting audio: same-speaker cosine median 0.25-0.51 (p5 0.099), different-speaker median -0.02 (p95 0.074, max 0.107). Separates people well; the operating point is far below the sherpa default of 0.5.

speakerModels.name: WeSpeaker CAM++ (large-margin), English
speakerModels.measured: 2026-08-12: same-speaker median 0.27, different-speaker median 0.30 (p95 0.53) on the same audio — the two distributions overlap, so it separated speakers WORSE than TitaNet here. Not recommended without your own measurement.

speakerModels.name: WeSpeaker ResNet293 (large-margin), English
speakerModels.measured: 2026-08-12: every similarity runs high — same-speaker median 0.84-0.93 but different-speaker median 0.54 (p95 0.74). Needs a much higher threshold than the others and the tails still overlap; it looked perfect on single-speaker audio alone, which is why a same-speaker-only test is not sufficient evidence.

speakerModels.name: No speaker model (transcription only, no diarization)

thresholdNote: recommendedThreshold is per model and NOT interchangeable: cosine similarity scales differ between embedders. Changing the speaker model without re-measuring its operating point will either fragment one speaker into many or merge several into one.

segmentationModels.name: pyannote segmentation 3.0 (speaker turn and overlap detection)
segmentationModels.note: Converted to ONNX by k2-fsa from the gated pyannote/segmentation-3.0 weights and redistributed ungated with the upstream MIT licence file, so no Hugging Face token is needed. Detects speaker turns and overlap inside one endpointed utterance, which raw embeddings cannot do reliably at short durations.

segmentationModels.name: No turn detection (one speaker per endpointed utterance)
